title: Hydraulic machine station with clamping and working linear motions
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Fixed-displacement open-circuit hydraulic supply with tank, pump, global relief, and one shared open-center 4/3 DCV. DCV.A is the extend command line: it feeds the clamp cap/holding branch through a pressure-reducing valve and dual pilot-operated check load lock, and it also feeds the forward sequence valve. The forward sequence valve is externally piloted from the reduced clamp holding line, so the working cylinder cap is supplied only after clamp pressure is established. DCV.B is the retract command line: it directly supplies the working cylinder rod and also feeds/pilots the reverse sequence valve. The reverse sequence valve supplies a second pressure-reducing valve for the clamp rod/release branch only after working retract pressure rises at end of retraction. Both clamp work-port feeds are therefore reduced below the global system pressure ceiling. Open-center neutral unloads the fixed pump and vents both work lines to tank so clamp load-lock pilot pressure can decay. No flow-control valves are included because all speed realizations are sizing_only.

function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank.S feeds Pump.S; Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P and DCV.P; ReliefValve.T and DCV.T return to Tank.R. The fixed pump is unloaded by the open-center DCV neutral and protected by the relief valve.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: pressure-reduced clamp branch with actuator-port dual pilot-operated check and delayed release
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: DCV.A supplies the clamp cap through ClampExtendPressureReducingValve and ClampLoadLock for extension to force. ReverseSequenceValve supplies ClampReleasePressureReducingValve only after the working retract pressure condition, and that valve then supplies the clamp rod side through the load lock. Both clamp work-port feeds are pressure-reduced and drained/relieved to Tank.R. The dual pilot-operated check locks the clamp actuator ports for holding, while open-center neutral vents work lines for pilot decay.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: sizing-only double-acting cylinder advance/retract with forward pressure sequence
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: DCV.A feeds ForwardSequenceValve.P and, once clamp pressure at ForwardSequenceValve.X opens it, supplies WorkCylinder.Cap for advance. DCV.B directly supplies WorkCylinder.Rod for retraction. Cylinder areas and pump flow are deferred to sizing; no flow-control component is used.

The forward sequence valve opens the working cap feed only when the clamp reduced-pressure holding line is live and has reached the set pressure. This hydraulically inhibits working advance until clamp pressure is established without using an electrical pressure switch.

On retract command, DCV.B supplies the working rod directly and supplies/pilots ReverseSequenceValve. Clamp release remains blocked until working retract pressure rises enough to open ReverseSequenceValve; after that release flow passes through ClampReleasePressureReducingValve to keep the clamp release/retract branch within the clamp pressure limit before reaching the clamp rod/load-lock release side.

design_decisions.decision: Use one shared directional valve for clamp and work sequencing.
design_decisions.rationale: A single DCV keeps the prerequisite clamp branch commanded while the sequenced working branch is enabled; separate independently commanded valves would make ordering a control-wiring property rather than a hydraulic interlock.

design_decisions.decision: Select an open-center 4/3 DCV with a fixed-displacement pump.
design_decisions.rationale: Open-center neutral unloads the fixed pump and vents both work lines, which supports pilot-operated check reseating and avoids holding pilot pressure trapped in neutral.

design_decisions.decision: Use pressure-reducing valves with reverse checks in both clamp work-port feeds.
design_decisions.rationale: The clamp branch has a lower pressure limit than the overall system ceiling. The extend/holding feed and the release/retract feed both receive reducing/relieving valves with drains to tank, so neither clamp chamber feed is exposed to the global relief setting as its normal pressure limit. Integral reverse checks preserve return flow through the opposite clamp line.

design_decisions.decision: Use externally piloted sequence valves for both forward and reverse hydraulic interlocks.
design_decisions.rationale: The forward sequence valve is piloted from the reduced clamp holding line, not from the common pump line, so it represents clamp pressure establishment. The reverse sequence valve is piloted from the working retract pressure line and delays clamp release until working retraction has produced the pressure condition.

design_decisions.decision: Do not add flow-control valves for the specified motion times.
design_decisions.rationale: All typed speed decisions are sizing_only. For horizontal resistive cylinders, nominal speeds can be met by pump-flow and cylinder-area sizing unless adjustability, load-independent speed, or overrunning-load restraint is required.

research_coverage.summary: The evidence is strong for the generic hydraulic power unit/relief/return path, pressure-reduced clamp branch, pilot-operated-check load holding, and basic sequence-valve clamp-then-work advance. However, critical sequencing/interlock behavior is not yet safely and unambiguously covered. The findings include a warning that pressure-only sequence circuits can falsely advance the working actuator if clamp pressure rises before real part contact, and the accumulated connection guidance does not yet detail the reverse-return interlock needed to keep the clamp applied until the working axis has retracted. More targeted evidence is needed before topology design can proceed safely.

items.rationale: Findings support a complete open hydraulic power path: reservoir to pump suction, pump pressure line through directional valves or regulated branches, return to tank, and a system relief valve from pressure line to reservoir for overpressure protection. They also distinguish fixed-displacement/open-center and pressure-controlled/closed-center arrangements.

Findings support using a 4-way directional-control valve to command a cylinder in a two-cylinder clamp/work sequence, including shifted flow to actuator work ports and return flow to tank. They also identify the required neutral behavior when pilot-operated checks are used: work ports/pilot lines must be drained so the checks reseat, rather than relying on a leaking closed spool for holding.

Findings support leak-resistant holding at the clamp actuator using pilot-operated check/load-lock style valves in the cylinder work-port lines, cross-piloted from the opposite work line, with directional-valve neutral arranged to drain pilot ports. Evidence also warns that closed directional spool sealing alone is not acceptable for load holding because spool leakage can cause drift.

Findings support a working-axis cylinder controlled by a shared 4-way directional valve in a two-cylinder sequence circuit. The cited sequence-valve source states one 4-way directional valve can control both cylinders through extend and retract phases, while the generic open-circuit evidence describes how shifted directional valves route pump flow to one actuator port and return flow from the opposite port to tank.

Forward automatic transition from clamp to working advance is supported by a normally closed sequence valve in the working branch, opening after clamp pressure rises. Flow-based speed sizing for resistive loads is also supported. The weak point is the return-phase motion profile/interlock: the findings cite that a two-cylinder sequence can be cylinder 1 extend, cylinder 2 extend, cylinder 2 retract, cylinder 1 retract, but they do not extract enough connection/placement logic to show how the working axis is forced to retract before clamp release in the requested topology.

A pressure sequence valve pattern for clamp-then-work advance is supported, including placement in the secondary actuator line, inlet/upstream pressure sensing, external drain, and reverse-flow check where needed. However, the evidence itself states that a sequence circuit may falsely allow the second actuator to cycle if clamp pressure builds before actual part contact. Therefore the proof-of-clamp/precondition interlock is not safely covered. Reverse interlock connection logic for working retract before clamp retract is also not sufficiently detailed.

Findings support using a pressure-reducing valve, not only a relief valve, to maintain a lower secondary clamp-branch pressure. Evidence covers placement in the branch or actuator line, downstream pressure sensing, open drain to tank, and the need to keep the main system relief for overall protection while setting the reducing valve to the lower clamp limit.

Static leak-resistant clamp holding and holding after the sequence valve opens are supported by pilot-operated checks/load-lock valves in the clamp cylinder line. What remains weak is the complete interlocked return behavior: the evidence does not yet show a supported connection pattern that keeps the clamp applied until the working axis has fully retracted and only then releases/unclamps.

design_issues.description: The forward sequence valve provides the required hydraulic pressure-dependent clamp-force-established signal without an electrical pressure switch, but pressure rise alone is not independent proof of actual workpiece contact or clamp position. This is acceptable under the stated brief because a pressure-dependent transition is requested, but it should be confirmed by machine risk assessment if part-presence proof is later required.

The reverse-order interlock topology is functionally plausible: DCV.B directly retracts the working cylinder while a reverse sequence valve delays clamp release until retract pressure rises. Final detailed design should verify the selected sequence-valve pilot source, setting, and reverse/free-flow behavior with valve application data, because the research notes did not include a detailed independent source for this exact reverse plumbing.

design_review.summary: No blocking functional topology errors found. The circuit uses one shared directional valve, direct global relief, reduced clamp feeds with drains, actuator-port clamp load locking, hydraulic forward pressure sequencing, and reverse-order hydraulic sequencing. Extend/retract and return paths are represented for both actuators, clamp holding is not dependent on DCV leakage, no unjustified flow-control valves are added, and the explicit no-electrical-pressure-switch requirement is met.

validation.summary: Deterministic validation: valid. Engineering review: valid. No blocking functional topology errors found. The circuit uses one shared directional valve, direct global relief, reduced clamp feeds with drains, actuator-port clamp load locking, hydraulic forward pressure sequencing, and reverse-order hydraulic sequencing. Extend/retract and return paths are represented for both actuators, clamp holding is not dependent on DCV leakage, no unjustified flow-control valves are added, and the explicit no-electrical-pressure-switch requirement is met.

policy.approach: Smallest evaluated design that proves all acceptance criteria: 80 mm clamp cylinder and deliberately upsized 125 mm working cylinder so standard pump flow stays within the approximate advance-speed band.

actuator_decisions.justification: Clamp extend/hold is the governing clamp load case. Sizing near the upper part of the 40 bar clamp branch allowance selects the preferred 80 mm bore without wasting pressure headroom.

The working advance force is governing. The lower design pressure intentionally moves selection to the 125 mm preferred bore, which the verifier showed keeps advance speed proven inside the tolerance band with the standard pump.

supply_decision.justification: Working advance is the only phase with a quantified speed requirement. The resulting 28.0 cm3/rev pump gives 37.8 L/min and the evaluated working-advance velocity is 3.080221106623306 m/min.

setting_decisions.basis: Set at the clamp branch pressure ceiling from the phase requirements.
Set at the same clamp branch pressure ceiling so the clamp release feed is also limited.
Set near the clamp design pressure: above the pressure chosen to represent established clamp force and below the system relief.
Set near the working-axis design pressure so clamp release waits for the working-axis retract pressure condition and remains below relief.
